messages:
Priya: RFC follow-up: KV shard decompression + tenant-aware cache extraction. TL;DR: split the monolithic kv-store into per-tenant logical shards and pull eviction/metrics into a small Cache Control service. Goal: reduce noisy-neighbor tail latency and make cache ownership explicit for long-term paydown. Looking for ops/infra tradeoffs and rollout suggestions.

Ethan: nice. first question: are we changing the data model or just the routing/ownership?

Priya: routing/ownership only. keys stay the same. we'll add a tenant prefix & a shard map to route reads/writes. migration is read-through with write mirroring during validation.

Rina: how will we handle hot tenants? will they get dedicated shards or autoscaled pools?

Priya: option A: sticky shard per-tenant (good isolation, more capacity). Option B: pool-of-shards with affinity (better packing). leaning to sticky for top 50 tenants, pool for rest.

Carlos: ops concerns: cross-shard transactions. we have a few flows that rely on multi-key atomicity. need to enumerate and create compensators.

Priya: noted. adding a migration checklist item to detect multi-key patterns and create compensator handlers.

Ethan: what about metrics and debugging? moving cache logic out will change spans and logs. ops will need a mapping layer in tracing to stitch requests.

Rina: add a small sidecar shim that emits the old-span id for a transitional period. once cutover we can remove it.

Carlos: rollout idea: 1) Dry-run routing -> mirror reads to new shards, 2) Warm caches with backfill, 3) Flip read traffic for cohort tenants, 4) Promote writes after 72h validation.

Priya: exact runbook (draft):

```
phase-0: discovery
- list hot keys, multi-key transactions, tenants by qps
phase-1: shard-map & shim
- deploy shard-map service + routing shim (feature-flagged)
- mirror reads to target shard, write-through remains to monolith
phase-2: warm & validate
- run cache backfill jobs per-tenant, collect hit-rate & tail latency
phase-3: cohort flip
- flip 5 low-risk tenants -> 48h observe
- if OK expand x5 each week
phase-4: write promote
- enable writes to new shards for cohort, keep mirror until 7d stable
phase-5: deprecate
- switch 100%, retire monolith keys, plan DB compaction
```

Carlos: please include automated rollback triggers: p99 latency > baseline * 1.5 OR error-rate > baseline + 0.5%.

Rina: add a chaos validation step (inject 250ms latency into shard service) and ensure upstream falls back gracefully.

Ethan: cost note: per-tenant sticky shards will increase memory footprint. need a rough delta for finance. Carlos / ops, can you produce a monthly estimate for sticky vs pooled?

Carlos: will do. initial estimate: sticky top-50 -> +20% mem, pooled -> +8%. rough numbers only.

Priya: compatibility concerns: existing services expect a consistent cache eviction policy. Cache Control service needs feature flags for eviction strategy per-tenant, defaulting to LRU. config example: 

```
cache-control:
  default_policy: LRU
  tenant_overrides:
    tenant-42: TTL-30m
    tenant-gamma: LFU
```

Rina: love tenant_overrides. also require contract tests for eviction behaviour so adapters don't regress.

Ethan: how long do we support dual writes? storage cost & complexity. I'd push for auto-cutover with staged validation to limit dual-write window to 7-14 days.

Priya: agreed. dual-write window 7d target, max 21d with exec approval. will add to RFC.

ops-bot: rfc-notify: RFC updated at https://redwood.internal/rfcs/PR-712 (Priya). Tagging @infra and @sre for approval.

Carlos: risk matrix (short):
- Risk: noisy neighbor persists -> Mitigation: dedicated shards + throttles
- Risk: data divergence during mirroring -> Mitigation: consistency checks + background reconciler
- Risk: increased ops surface -> Mitigation: small Cache Control team + runbooks + automations

Rina: acceptance gates:
- no more than 7% increase in p95 for any tenant during cohort
- cache-hit rate for cohort >= 70% after warm phase

Ethan: please add a log/trace guide: new span names, how to correlate old->new entries. makes debugging much easier.

Priya: will include trace mapping + sample dashboards (hit-rate, miss-cost, p95/p99, write-lag). thanks for feedback. I'll update RFC and ping infra ops for the cost delta.

Carlos: one last ops ask: automated cutback via route-police with TTL-based freeze. manual cutbacks = last resort.

Priya: good call. adding automated route-police rollback. thanks all, will post next revision tomorrow.
